newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Graboplast denies holding hazardous waste.
newsitem.headline: Graboplast denies holding hazardous waste.

text.p: Hungarian home improvement product maker Graboplast group on Tuesday denied it held large amounts of hazardous waste at its plants.

Company spokesman Gabor Baksa said that according to Graboplast's information, the police had started an investigation after it had found materials, allegedly including hazardous waste, on a Graboplast truck last weekend.
Graboplast spokesman Gabor Baksa told Reuters the group had some 100 tonnes of waste from production.
"But this is not hazardous," he said. "It is just the same than when used wallpaper or plastic floor is taken to the waste disposal site as communal waste."
Baksa said the case had initially been sparked by an unsigned letter to the environmental authority.

Graboplast's share price fell from 4,700 forints to 4,550 on the Budapest Stock Exchange last week, and dropped further after the first news about the waste, closing at 4,380 forints on Monday. But on Tuesday the stock rose and ended at 4,425.
